I think the cleanest answer is the taxonomy-collapse one, and I’d resist treating the Agrippa regress as the central pair here. Regress/circularity is a general problem for any theory that demands justification; it arises only once one assumes every justifier must itself be justified. But the question’s special constraint is narrower and more damaging: if the only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, then JTB cannot keep justification and truth as independent conditions. That yields two distinct problems:

1. Justified false belief. JTB entails that a belief can be justified yet false. Such a belief is not Knowledge, so on a K/B-only taxonomy it must fall into mere Belief. But so does unjustified false belief. Thus justification is invisible in the false case; a responsibly held error is classified exactly like a random false belief.

2. Unjustified true belief. JTB entails that a belief can be true yet unjustified—a lucky guess, wishful thinking, etc. It is not Knowledge, so it too must fall into mere Belief. But so does false belief. Thus truth is invisible in the non-knowledge case; a lucky true belief is classified exactly like a false belief.

So JTB’s own three conditions collapse: the only positive cell is J&T&B = Knowledge, and all other combinations are an undifferentiated Belief. The regress or circularity can be a downstream consequence of trying to make justification another K/B item, but it is not one of the two direct JTB problems under the stated K/B-only taxonomy. The two problems are the loss of justified false belief as a distinct status and the loss of unjustified true belief as a distinct status. That is why colleagues 3, 4, 8, 10, 11, and 12 have the right diagnosis.

I think the discussion has isolated the right first problem but is beginning to double-count the second. The unavoidable first problem is the regress of justification: if justification must be cashed out using only Knowledge and Belief, then each justifier is either another belief needing support or an already-known belief whose own justification is again in question. Circularity is important here, but it should not be treated as a separate problem. A circle of beliefs justifying each other is simply the regress that loops rather than continues; it is one horn of the same Agrippa-style dilemma, not an additional structural cost.

The second distinct problem is the collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy. On JTB, Knowledge = Justified & True & Belief. If everything that is not Knowledge must be mere Belief, then justified false belief, unjustified true belief, and unjustified false belief all occupy one undifferentiated category. Justification becomes invisible when truth fails, and truth becomes invisible when justification fails. This is independent of how we handle the regress: even if we somehow stop the justificatory chain, the K/B-only framework still cannot represent the difference between a well-supported error and a lucky true guess. So I would frame the two problems as (1) the regress of justification and (2) the collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy, with circularity treated as a variant of the regress rather than a separate second problem.

I think the discussion is splitting because several items are being treated as separate problems when they are really one horn of the same difficulty. Under JTB, \(Kp \iff Bp \land Tp \land Jp\). If the only epistemic states available are Knowledge and Belief, then \(Jp\) cannot be a primitive third state. Any justifier must be either a further belief or a piece of knowledge; and since knowledge itself includes justified belief, even a K-justifier just reintroduces the need for justification. That gives the justificatory-chain problem: an endless regress, or a loop/circle, or an arbitrary stopping point. But circularity and arbitrary foundations are not independent second problems; they are alternative ways the same regress horn fails to terminate non-arbitrarily.

The genuinely distinct second problem is the collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy. JTB requires truth and justification to remain independently trackable. With only K and B, however, the space collapses: \(T \land J\) is Knowledge, while \(J \land \neg T\), \(\neg J \land T\), and \(\neg J \land \neg T\) are all just “Belief.” So justified false belief and unjustified true belief lose their distinct status. That is not just another version of the regress; it is the representational inadequacy of a binary K/B ontology for a tripartite JTB analysis.

So I would frame the two non-Gettier problems as: (1) infinite regress of justification, with circularity and arbitrary stopping points as subcases of that failure; and (2) collapse of the K/B taxonomy into an undifferentiated catch-all Belief. Counting circularity as a separate second problem risks double-counting one justificatory-chain issue and missing the independent taxonomy problem.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The constraint “only epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief” makes the expressive cost of JTB the salient issue. On JTB Kp iff Bp & Tp & Jp the 2×2 J×T space is in principle

* JT = Knowledge
* J¬T = justified false belief
* ¬J T = unjustified / lucky true belief
* ¬J ¬T = unjustified false belief

With only K and unqualified B as tags the first cell is Knowledge and the other three are forced into one residual ‘Belief’. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction JFB ∨ UTB ∨ UFB.

The consensus in round 0 and round 1 that I am tracking is therefore a taxonomy collapse with two mirror costs:

1. Justification without truth is invisible. J & B & ¬T is a justified false belief. It is epistemically good in being responsibly held but ¬T so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a K/B only ontology it must be called mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J & B & ¬T and with ¬J & B & T. No distinct state of justified belief exists; a rational error is epistemically indistinguishable from an irrational false belief, and justification can only be marked when truth is present.

2. Truth without justification is invisible. ¬J & T & B is an unjustified true belief, a lucky hit. It is true but ¬J so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a K/B only ontology it must also be called mere Belief and is lumped with J & B & ¬T and with ¬J & B & ¬T. No distinct state of true/accidental belief exists; a lucky true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a false belief, and truth can only be marked when justification is present.

Colleagues 1,13,14,2,6 also present the dynamic consequence of the same binary ontology: with no independent ‘justified belief’ attitude Jp has to be reconstrued as Bp or Kp, so the justifier chain drives Agrippa’s trilemma. In that framing the two problems are often stated as infinite regress of justification and arbitrary/dogmatic foundational stopping point, with circularity treated as a looped variant of regress rather than a separate problem. Colleagues 5 and 7 push regress + arbitrary foundation / basing/access as the core pair, arguing taxonomy collapse is downstream.

Unresolved for me after round 1: the exam phrasing points strongly to the heterogeneity/collapse formulation, i.e. the two mixed cases JFB vs UTB, which itself entails the regress/foundation difficulty. * J & T & B = Knowledge
* J & ¬T & B = justified false belief
* ¬J & T & B = unjustified / lucky true belief
* ¬J & ¬T & B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge and unqualified Belief as predicates, the first cell is Knowledge and the remaining three are forced into ‘Belief’. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction JFB ∨ UTB ∨ UFB.

1. Justification without truth is invisible. J & B & ¬T is not Knowledge because ¬T, so on K/B only it is mere Belief, lumped with ¬J & B & ¬T and ¬J & B & T. No distinct state of justified belief; a rational error is indistinguishable from an irrational false belief. Justification can only be marked when truth is present.

No distinct state of true / accidental belief; a lucky hit is indistinguishable from false belief and from justified false belief. Truth can only be marked when justification is present.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we should consolidate rather than keep multiplying the Agrippa horns. The first issue is the justificatory-chain failure. - \(J \land \neg T \land B =\) justified false belief
- \(\neg J \land T \land B =\) unjustified true belief

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the most stable synthesis is now the one C1, C13, and C14 are converging on, and it also accommodates the matrix point made by C10–C12. The two non-Gettier problems are: (1) the infinite regress/failure of non-arbitrary termination in justification, and (2) the collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy. Circularity should not be counted as a separate second problem here; it is just the looped form of the same justificatory-chain failure. Likewise, an arbitrary foundational stopping point is not an independent second problem—it is the other way the first horn fails to terminate. If we counted circularity and arbitrary foundation separately, we would be multiplying Agrippa horns rather than answering the question’s two-problem structure.

C9’s objection that regress is “general” underestimates why the K/B-only constraint makes it structurally unavoidable. If justification is not an independent epistemic state, then a justifier for p must be either another Belief or a piece of Knowledge. If it is merely another Belief, it needs further support; if it is Knowledge, it already contains justification and so reopens the demand at a higher level. That is not a generic background worry; it is forced by the JTB definition plus the K/B-only ontology.

The second problem is genuinely distinct from the regress: even if we somehow stopped the justificatory chain, the K/B taxonomy still cannot represent the JTB matrix. Knowledge is \(J \land T \land B\); everything else is forced into “Belief.” So \(J \land \neg T \land B\) (justified false belief) and \(\neg J \land T \land B\) (unjustified true belief) lose their distinct status, along with ordinary unjustified false belief. Justification becomes invisible when truth fails, and truth becomes invisible when justification fails. That is not another version of the regress; it is the expressive failure of a binary K/B ontology for a tripartite JTB analysis.

So I would formulate the final answer as: the two problems are the regress of justification and the collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy, with circularity and arbitrary foundations treated as subcases of the first problem rather than as additional independent problems.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’d consolidate the discussion around the hybrid rather than either the taxonomy-only or Agrippa-only readings. The strongest formal point is that JTB requires justification and truth to remain independently trackable, but with only Knowledge and Belief the \(J \times T\) space collapses:

- \(J \land T \land B =\) Knowledge
- \(J \land \neg T \land B\), \(\neg J \land T \land B\), and \(\neg J \land \neg T \land B\) all become mere Belief.

So justified false belief and unjustified true belief lose their distinct status. That is an independent representational failure of the K/B-only taxonomy.

But C9’s taxonomy-only line is incomplete. If Knowledge and Belief are the only epistemic states, then \(Jp\) cannot be a primitive third state. A justifier must be either another Belief or a piece of Knowledge. If it is another Belief, it needs further justification; if it is Knowledge, it already contains justification and so reopens the same demand at a higher level. That yields the justificatory-chain problem: regress or termination failure. Circularity and arbitrary stopping points are not separate second problems; they are just alternative ways the same chain fails to terminate non-arbitrarily.

So the clean two-problem formulation is:

1. Infinite regress/termination failure of justification, with circularity and arbitrary foundations as variants of that same horn.
2. Collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy, because justified false beliefs and lucky true beliefs have no distinct home outside Knowledge.

Counting circularity as a separate second problem double-counts the justificatory-chain issue and leaves out the independent taxonomy collapse. I’d avoid that and keep the final answer as regress/termination failure plus K/B taxonomy collapse.

6.text:
With Knowledge = B∧T∧J and the only doxastic labels K and unqualified B, the J×T space that JTB itself commits to cannot be marked independently of the K/B divide.

On the JTB matrix with B presupposed

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified / lucky true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

the first cell is the only one that can be named as distinct. The residual
label ‘Belief’ is forced to be

Belief = J∧B∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧B∧T ∨ ¬J∧B∧¬T

i.e. a heterogeneous catch-all in which justification and truth can only be registered together.

That collapse is two-sided.

1. Justification without truth is invisible. J∧B∧¬T is a justified false belief. It is epistemically good in being responsibly held but ¬T so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a strict K/B inventory it must be called mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J∧B∧¬T and with ¬J∧B∧T. A rational error is therefore indistinguishable from an irrational error. Justification can be marked only when truth is present; there is no distinct state of justified belief in the false domain.

2. Truth without justification is invisible. ¬J∧B∧T is an unjustified true belief, a lucky hit. It is true but ¬J so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a strict K/B inventory it must also be called mere Belief and is lumped with J∧B∧¬T and with ¬J∧B∧¬T. A lucky true belief is therefore indistinguishable from a false belief, justified or not. Truth can be marked only when justification is present; there is no distinct state of true/accidental belief in the non-knowledge domain.

Hence JTB can only register justification when truth is present and can only register truth when justification is present. The classic intermediate normative positions JFB and UTB have no home and Belief = JFB ∨ UTB ∨ UFB.

That taxonomic cost is the structural expression of the justificatory-chain worry. With no independent attitude for justification, Jp must be reconstrued as Kp or Bp, so a justifier is either a further belief needing support or a piece of knowledge whose own justification is again in question. The familiar Agrippa trilemma, regress / loop / dogmatic stopping point, is just the dynamic form of the same collapse: any stopping point under a K/B only ontology is mere Belief, i.e. the unjustified foundation the taxonomy already makes invisible.

8.text:
With a strict K/B ontology JTB can only mark the conjunction

K p  iff  B p & T p & J p

and everything else is forced into the unqualified residual Belief.

On the J×T space with B presupposed you have in principle

* J & T & B = Knowledge
* J & ¬T & B = justified false belief
* ¬J & T & B = unjustified / lucky true belief
* ¬J & ¬T & B = unjustified false belief

If Knowledge and unqualified Belief are the only attitude predicates that are
available the first cell is the only one that can be marked off as distinct.
Belief = J&B&¬T ∨ ¬J&B&T ∨ ¬J&B&¬T is then a heterogeneous catch-all and
justification and truth can only be registered together.

That collapse has two independent sides, both pre-Gettier.

1. Justification without truth is invisible. J & B & ¬T is a justified false
belief. It is epistemically good in the sense of being responsibly held, but
¬T so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it must
be called mere Belief and is lumped together with ¬J&B&¬T and with ¬J&B&T.
Justification can be marked only when truth is present. There is no distinct
state of justified belief: a rational error is epistemically indistinguishable
from an irrational error and a justified false belief has no home.

2. Truth without justification is invisible. ¬J & B & T is an unjustified true
belief, a lucky hit. It is true but ¬J so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a
Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief and is
lumped together with J&B&¬T and with ¬J&B&¬T. Truth can be marked only when
justification is present. There is no distinct state of true/accidental belief:
a lucky true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a false belief,
justified or not, and truth is invisible in the non-knowledge domain.

Hence JTB can only register justification when truth is present and can only
register truth when justification is present. Justified false belief and
unjustified true belief have no distinct epistemic place and are both
downgraded to unqualified Belief. That is the representational inadequacy of a
binary K/B ontology for a tripartite JTB analysis. The familiar Agrippa
regress/foundation difficulty is the dynamic expression of the same collapse:
with no independent ‘justified belief’ attitude Jp must be reconstrued as Bq or
Kq, so justification is forced to be built out of further beliefs/knowledge.

10.text:
With a strict Knowledge / Belief ontology JTB can only mark one positive cell

K p  iff  B p & J p & T p

and everything else is forced into the residual unqualified Belief

B p  ≡  ¬[J p & T p & B p]  ≡  J p & B p & ¬T p  ∨  ¬J p & B p & T p  ∨  ¬J p & B p & ¬T p

Hence Belief is a heterogeneous catch-all and justification and truth can only be registered together. The 2x2 J x T space that JTB itself commits to collapses to K vs B.

1. Justification without truth is invisible. J & B & ¬T is a justified false belief. It is epistemically good in being responsibly held, but ¬T so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a K/B only inventory it must be called mere Belief and is lumped together with ¬J & B & ¬T and with ¬J & B & T. Justification can therefore be marked only when truth is present. A rational error is epistemically indistinguishable from an irrational false belief; there is no distinct state of justified belief, i.e. JFB has no home.

2. Truth without justification is invisible. ¬J & B & T is an unjustified / lucky true belief. It is true but held by luck, accident or wishful thinking, ¬J so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a K/B only inventory it must also be called mere Belief and is lumped together with J & B & ¬T and ¬J & B & ¬T. Truth can therefore be marked only when justification is present. A lucky hit is epistemically indistinguishable from a false belief and from a justified false belief; there is no distinct state of true but accidental belief, i.e. UTB has no home.

Hence on a binary K/B ontology you can say a belief is justified only if it is also true, and you can say a belief is true only if it is also justified. JTB’s own intermediate normative positions – a responsibly held error and a lucky hit – are forced into the undifferentiated category of mere Belief. That is the pre-Gettier expressive failure.

The dynamic expression of the same collapse is the justificatory-chain problem. With no independent ‘justified belief’ attitude Jp must be reconstrued as Bp or Kp. That drives the familiar Agrippa regress: each justifier is a further belief needing support, which either generates an infinite regress, loops in circularity, or stops arbitrarily in a basic mere Belief that is not Knowledge. The regress / arbitrary foundation worry is therefore the structural consequence of the taxonomic collapse: justification and truth cannot be given an independent home outside the Knowledge cell.

Hence justification and truth can only be registered together, in Knowledge.

A responsibly held error is therefore lumped together with ¬J & B & ¬T and with ¬J & B & T. Justification can be marked only when truth is present. There is no distinct state of true / accidental belief; an unjustified true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a false belief and from a justified false belief.

JFB and UTB have no home. JTB can only register justification when truth is present and can only register truth when justification is present. That is the pre-Gettier expressive cost of a binary K/B ontology. The familiar Agrippa regress / arbitrary foundation worry is the dynamic expression of the same collapse: with no independent ‘justified belief’ attitude Jp must be reconstrued as Bq or Kq, so a justifier either generates an endless chain of justifying beliefs, loops, or stops arbitrarily in a merely believed basic.

I think we are very close to a clean consolidation. The two problems should be:

1. **The justificatory regress/termination failure.** If Knowledge and Belief are the only available epistemic states, justification cannot be an independent third state. So any justifier for a belief must be either another belief, which needs its own justification, or a piece of knowledge, whose justificatory status already includes the very thing being demanded. That generates an endless chain. Circularity is not a separate second problem here; it is just the looped version of the same failure. Likewise, arbitrary or dogmatic stopping points are the other terminal failure of the same chain. They are subcases of the regress/termination horn, not independent items.

JTB needs justification and truth to remain independently trackable, but with only K and B, the only positive cell is \(J \land T \land B = K\), while \(J \land \neg T\), \(\neg J \land T\), and \(\neg J \land \neg T\) all fall into the single residual category “Belief.” So justified false belief and unjustified true belief lose their distinct status. Colleague 9’s two points are right in substance, but they should be consolidated as one problem: the residual category Belief becomes a heterogeneous catch-all. The loss of justified false belief and the loss of lucky true belief are two sides of the same taxonomic collapse, not two separate problems.

So I would resist both moves that threaten the clean answer: don’t list circularity as a separate second problem, because that double-counts the termination issue; and don’t drop the regress, because the K/B-only constraint is precisely what makes justification impossible to stop non-arbitrarily. The final formulation should be: **(1) infinite regress of justification, with circularity and arbitrary stopping as subcases, and (2) collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy into an undifferentiated Belief category.**

I think we should consolidate rather than keep multiplying the Agrippa horns. The first issue is the justificatory-chain failure. Under a strict K/B inventory, \(Jp\) cannot be an independent state, so a justifier must be either \(Bq\) or \(Kq\). If it is \(Bq\), \(q\) itself needs justification, producing an endless regress. If it is \(Kq\), then \(Kq\) already includes \(Jq\), so the demand for justification is either restarted at a higher level or loops back. So infinite regress is the central first problem; circularity and arbitrary stopping points are best treated as variants of that same termination failure, not as a separate second problem.

The genuinely independent second problem is the collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy. JTB commits us to the \(J \times T\) matrix:

- \(J \land T \land B =\) Knowledge
- \(J \land \neg T \land B =\) justified false belief
- \(\neg J \land T \land B =\) unjustified true belief
- \(\neg J \land \neg T \land B =\) unjustified false belief

But with only Knowledge and Belief as available labels, only the first cell can be marked as Knowledge. The other three are all forced into “Belief.” So justified false belief and unjustified true belief lose their distinct status: justification becomes invisible when truth fails, and truth becomes invisible when justification fails. That is not just another version of the regress; even if the justificatory chain were somehow stopped, the binary taxonomy still could not represent a rational error versus a lucky true guess.

So I would frame the final two problems as: (1) infinite regress/termination failure of justification, with circularity as a subcase rather than a separate item, and (2) collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy into an undifferentiated catch-all Belief. The two taxonomy symptoms are the two sides of one collapse, not two additional problems.

I’d consolidate the discussion around the hybrid rather than either the taxonomy-only or Agrippa-only readings. The strongest formal point is that JTB requires justification and truth to remain independently trackable, but with only Knowledge and Belief the \(J \times T\) space collapses:

- \(J \land T \land B =\) Knowledge
- \(J \land \neg T \land B\), \(\neg J \land T \land B\), and \(\neg J \land \neg T \land B\) all become mere Belief.

So justified false belief and unjustified true belief lose their distinct status. That is an independent representational failure of the K/B-only taxonomy.

But C9’s taxonomy-only line is incomplete. If Knowledge and Belief are the only epistemic states, then \(Jp\) cannot be a primitive third state. A justifier must be either another Belief or a piece of Knowledge. If it is another Belief, it needs further justification; if it is Knowledge, it already contains justification and so reopens the same demand at a higher level. That yields the justificatory-chain problem: regress or termination failure. Circularity and arbitrary stopping points are not separate second problems; they are just alternative ways the same chain fails to terminate non-arbitrarily.

So the clean two-problem formulation is:

1. Infinite regress/termination failure of justification, with circularity and arbitrary foundations as variants of that same horn.
2. Collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy, because justified false beliefs and lucky true beliefs have no distinct home outside Knowledge.

Counting circularity as a separate second problem double-counts the justificatory-chain issue and leaves out the independent taxonomy collapse. I’d avoid that and keep the final answer as regress/termination failure plus K/B taxonomy collapse.

With Knowledge = B∧T∧J and the only doxastic labels K and unqualified B, the J×T space that JTB itself commits to cannot be marked independently of the K/B divide.

On the JTB matrix with B presupposed

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified / lucky true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

the first cell is the only one that can be named as distinct. The residual
label ‘Belief’ is forced to be

Belief = J∧B∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧B∧T ∨ ¬J∧B∧¬T

i.e. a heterogeneous catch-all in which justification and truth can only be registered together.

That collapse is two-sided.

1. Justification without truth is invisible. J∧B∧¬T is a justified false belief. It is epistemically good in being responsibly held but ¬T so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a strict K/B inventory it must be called mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J∧B∧¬T and with ¬J∧B∧T. A rational error is therefore indistinguishable from an irrational error. Justification can be marked only when truth is present; there is no distinct state of justified belief in the false domain.

2. Truth without justification is invisible. ¬J∧B∧T is an unjustified true belief, a lucky hit. It is true but ¬J so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a strict K/B inventory it must also be called mere Belief and is lumped with J∧B∧¬T and with ¬J∧B∧¬T. A lucky true belief is therefore indistinguishable from a false belief, justified or not. Truth can be marked only when justification is present; there is no distinct state of true/accidental belief in the non-knowledge domain.

Hence JTB can only register justification when truth is present and can only register truth when justification is present. The classic intermediate normative positions JFB and UTB have no home and Belief = JFB ∨ UTB ∨ UFB.

That taxonomic cost is the structural expression of the justificatory-chain worry. With no independent attitude for justification, Jp must be reconstrued as Kp or Bp, so a justifier is either a further belief needing support or a piece of knowledge whose own justification is again in question. The familiar Agrippa trilemma, regress / loop / dogmatic stopping point, is just the dynamic form of the same collapse: any stopping point under a K/B only ontology is mere Belief, i.e. the unjustified foundation the taxonomy already makes invisible.

The JTB analysis is K p ≡ B p ∧ T p ∧ J p. With only the epistemic labels Knowledge and unqualified Belief there is no independent attitude for justification or for truth. The 2×2 justification × truth space therefore collapses to two cells: J∧T∧B = Knowledge and ¬J∧T∧B, J∧¬T∧B, ¬J∧¬T∧B = all labelled Belief. That collapse is the core non-Gettier cost and is now the dominant framing in the discussion.

Two distinct non-knowledge positions are lost inside the undifferentiated Belief bucket:

1. Justification without truth – justified false belief, J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. It is responsibly held, epistemically good in the sense of justification, but not Knowledge because ¬T. On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it must be called mere Belief and is lumped with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. Justification becomes invisible in the false domain; rational error cannot be distinguished from irrational error. No distinct state of justified belief.

2. Truth without justification – unjustified true belief, ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. It is true but held by luck/accident and not Knowledge because ¬J. On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief and is lumped with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. Truth becomes invisible in the non-knowledge domain; a lucky hit cannot be distinguished from a false belief. No distinct state of true/accidental belief.

Hence Belief = JFB ∨ UTB ∨ UFB. JTB can only register justification when truth is present and truth when justification is present. This is the taxonomic price of reducing the ontology to K vs B, expressed by colleagues 10,11,12,3,4,6,8,2 as loss of justified belief and true belief as intermediate states.

A second, structurally related line is the dynamic consequence of having to build justification out of only K and B. Because J p can only be realised as K q or B q, justification must be provided by another belief/knowledge, yielding Agrippa: infinite regress of justifiers K p → K q → K r…; vicious circle; or a dogmatic stopping point where a basic belief is accepted without further justification. The stopping point can only be mere Belief under the binary taxonomy, so it is not Knowledge and the regress either never terminates or terminates in arbitrary unjustified foundation. Colleagues 1,13,14,9,5,7,2,6 stress regress/termination failure and arbitrary foundation / basing relation / access/factivity as the structural worry.

Infinite regress/termination failure of justification, with circularity and arbitrary/dogmatic foundation treated as subcases/variants of the same termination failure, not as a separate second problem. The J×T matrix with B presupposed is J T = Knowledge; J ¬T = justified false belief; ¬J T = unjustified/lucky true belief; ¬J ¬T = unjustified false belief. Round 2 shows a strong convergence on a hybrid two-problem synthesis, with the taxonomy collapse now being treated as the independent second problem and the justificatory-chain failure as the first.

2. Collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy – a pre-Gettier expressive failure. With only K/B labels Belief must do the work of three cells.

   a. Justification without truth is invisible. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is a justified false belief: epistemically good as responsibly held but ¬T so by JTB not Knowledge. Justification can therefore be marked only when truth is present; there is no distinct state of justified belief, JFB has no home.
* Truth without justification is invisible. ¬J∧B∧T is an unjustified true belief, a lucky hit. It is true but ¬J so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On a K/B only inventory it must also be called mere Belief and is lumped with J∧B∧¬T and ¬J∧B∧¬T. Truth can therefore be marked only when justification is present; there is no distinct state of true but accidental belief, UTB has no home.

That collapse is the formally independent second problem: even if the justificatory chain could be halted, the binary K/B ontology still could not represent the JTB matrix.

The dynamic expression of the same K/B-only constraint is the justificatory-chain problem. With no independent ‘justified belief’ attitude Jp must be reconstrued as Bq or Kq. If it is Bq, q itself needs support; if it is Kq, Kq already contains Jq and the demand reopens at a higher level. The JTB commitment under B-presupposed is K p iff B p ∧ T p ∧ J p. The only nameable cell is J T B; Belief = ¬[J∧T∧B] = J∧B∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧B∧T ∨ ¬J∧B∧¬T is a heterogeneous catch-all.

Round 3 shows strong convergence on a hybrid two-problem synthesis.

1. Justificatory-chain/termination failure. Jp cannot be a primitive third attitude under K/B-only ontology, so a justifier must be reconstrued as Bq or Kq. If Bq, q needs its own justification → endless regress; if Kq, Kq already contains Jq so demand reopens at higher level → loop. An arbitrary dogmatic stopping point in mere Belief is the failure to terminate. Infinite regress, circularity and arbitrary foundation are now treated as variants/subcases of the same termination failure, not a separate second problem. This is the dynamic expression of having no independent justified-belief state.

2. Collapse of the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy – pre-Gettier expressive failure. With only K/B labels Belief must do work of three cells.

a. Justification without truth invisible. J∧B∧¬T justified false belief is epistemically good as responsibly held but ¬T so not Knowledge. On K/B only it must be called mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J∧B∧¬T and ¬J∧B∧T. Justification can be marked only when truth is present; a rational error is indistinguishable from irrational false belief. JFB has no home.

b. Truth without justification invisible. ¬J∧B∧T unjustified/lucky true belief is true but ¬J so not Knowledge. On K/B only it must also be called mere Belief and is lumped with J∧B∧¬T and ¬J∧B∧¬T. Truth can be marked only when justification is present; a lucky hit is indistinguishable from false belief. UTB has no home.

Hence JTB can only register justification when truth is present and truth when justification is present. JFB and UTB are two sides of one taxonomic collapse; the regress/termination failure is its structural consequence.

The JTB analysis is K p ≡ B p ∧ T p ∧ J p. With only the epistemic labels Knowledge and unqualified Belief there is no independent attitude for justification or for truth. The 2×2 justification × truth space therefore collapses to two cells: J∧T∧B = Knowledge and ¬J∧T∧B, J∧¬T∧B, ¬J∧¬T∧B = all labelled Belief. That collapse is the core non-Gettier cost.

Two distinct non-knowledge positions are lost inside the undifferentiated Belief bucket:
1. Justification without truth – justified false belief, J∧B∧¬T. It is responsibly held but not Knowledge because ¬T. On K/B only it is lumped with unjustified false belief and unjustified true belief. Justification becomes invisible in the false domain; rational error cannot be distinguished from irrational error. No distinct state of justified belief.
2. Truth without justification – unjustified true belief, ¬J∧B∧T. It is true but held by luck/accident and not Knowledge because ¬J. On K/B only it is lumped with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. Truth becomes invisible in the non-knowledge domain; a lucky hit cannot be distinguished from a false belief. No distinct state of true/accidental belief.

Hence Belief = JFB ∨ UTB ∨ UFB. JTB can only register justification when truth is present and truth when justification is present. This is the taxonomic price of reducing the ontology to K vs B.

A second, structurally related line is the dynamic consequence of having to build justification out of only K and B. Because Jp can only be realised as Kq or Bq, justification must be provided by another belief/knowledge, yielding Agrippa: infinite regress of justifiers K p → K q → K r…; vicious circle; or a dogmatic stopping point where a basic belief is accepted without further justification. The stopping point can only be mere Belief under the binary taxonomy, so it is not Knowledge and the regress either never terminates or terminates in arbitrary unjustified foundation.

* J ¬T B = justified false belief
